newsitem.title: USA: U.S. official visits Sudan to look at human rights.
newsitem.headline: U.S. official visits Sudan to look at human rights.

text.p: A senior U.S. official is in Sudan to investigate the human rights situation there with special focus on religious persecution, a State Department spokesman said on Friday.

The spokeman said Deputy Assistant Secretary for Human Rights, Gare Smith, had met Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir, the justice minister and other government officials as well as human rights attorneys, religious and women's groups.
"He urged the government leaders to take a range of clear measures that would build international confidence in the government of Sudan and (their) human rights intentions," the spokesman said.

Smith, he said, had conveyed the U.S. government's concern about credible reports of religious persecution, slavery and female genital mutilation in Sudan. He would be in Sudan until Sunday after which he would visit Ethiopia.
